news.headline: Select Technologies raises Rs3.02bn through IPO, becomes 1st PSX listing of new fiscal year
news.summary: Select Technologies Limited, a Pakistani smartphone and consumer-appliances maker, raised Rs3.02bn via IPO of 88.9m ordinary shares (10% of post-issue paid-up capital); floor price Rs28.00/share, strike price discovered at Rs34.00/share (21% premium over floor) after book-building; issue oversubscribed 3.23x with ~13,000 investors participating (banks, mutual funds, insurers, pension funds, brokerages, HNWIs, retail). Not currently a KSE100/KMI30 universe constituent - logged for macro/primary-market sentiment context only; ticker symbol not confirmed in source reviewed.

news.headline: Dada Partners advises Nishat Group on Pakistan's largest private cross-border listed-company acquisition (Rafhan Maize)
news.summary: Nishat Group acquired 73.9% of Rafhan Maize Products Company Limited (RMPL) for approximately PKR 66 billion - 51% bought from majority shareholder Ingredion Incorporated (USA, which retains a strategic minority stake), 20.5% from a minority shareholder, and 2.4% via mandatory public offer - taking Nishat Group's total stake to a super-majority 75.9%; described in the article as the largest private-sector cross-border M&A of a listed Pakistani company, excluding privatizations. Dada Partners (Private) Limited was exclusive financial advisor to Nishat Group; Cornelius, Lane and Mufti (CLM) was legal counsel; Next Capital was Manager to the Offer.

news.headline: Hormuz tensions wipe out over 6,400 points at PSX - KSE-100 confirmed close
news.summary: Tuesday final close confirmed: Express Tribune reported KSE-100 'closed at 173,518.82, down 6,408.23 points, or 3.56%, from the previous close of 179,927.05, as selling intensified throughout the session'; volume 912.6m shares, value Rs45.6bn traded, 498 companies traded (40 up, 439 down, 19 unchanged); major decliners named: UBL, Engro Holdings, Fauji Fertiliser, Lucky Cement, Meezan Bank, OGDC, HBL, PPL and MCB Bank. Corroborating Dawn report (timestamped 3:00pm PKT) had the index at 173,839.01, down 6,088.03 points (-3.38%), quoting AKD Securities director of research Awais Ashraf: 'The decline is broad-based, with cyclical sectors witnessing the sharpest percentage losses amid heightened uncertainty over the medium-term outlook due to the emerging geopolitical situation.' Same Strait-of-Hormuz naval-blockade driver as prior entries this cycle; this is the deepest and now-final read of Tuesday's session, superseding the earlier intraday/delayed-quote entries logged above.

news.headline: Pakistan retires record Rs4.7tr debt ahead of maturity
news.summary: Pakistan retired Rs4.7 trillion (approx. $17bn) of public debt ahead of maturity - described as the largest early-retirement liability-management exercise in the country's history; composition 51% owed to SBP, 49% market debt/government securities; Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad called it the 'largest and most sustained liability management operation,' with average maturity of public debt extended from 2.7 years (FY24) to 3.8 years (FY26) - supportive for macro stability and refinancing risk, no direct PSX-ticker impact disclosed.

news.headline: PSX Opening Bell: Bulls Set the Early Pace
news.summary: Wednesday early trade (published 09:50am PKT), rebounding off Tuesday's 173,518.81 close: KSE-100 at 176,202.88, up 2,684.07 points (+1.55%), intraday high 176,344.73 (+2,825.92 pts); driver: 'investors engaged in value buying after heavy selloffs' in the prior session; breadth 89 advancers vs 6 decliners, 1 unchanged, 4 untraded of the 100 index companies, volume 21.22m shares; top % gainers YOUW +4.44%, SCBPL +3.82%, FATIMA +3.60%, KTML +3.37%, CHCC +3.31%; largest point contributors UBL +373.08, MEBL +170.87, ENGROH +156.53, FFC +148.66, HUBC +124.02.

news.headline: PSX Closing Bell: Every Rose Has Its Thorn
news.summary: Tuesday confirmed close detail (same Strait-of-Hormuz selloff already logged above at impact 5; this is Mettis's own closing-bell print, published Jul 14, 2026 4:03pm PKT, with sector breakdown not previously captured): KSE-100 closed at 173,518.81, down 6,408.23 points (-3.56%); volume 409.23m shares, value traded Rs45.61bn, 620,763 trades across 498 companies; breadth 40 higher, 439 lower, 19 unchanged; top losers GHNI -8.74%, TRG -8.21%, GAL -8.01%, AKBL -7.65%, MLCF -7.55%; sole listed top gainer UPFL +0.36%. Reason given: 'escalating geopolitical tensions and a surge in global oil prices' after Trump's 20% Hormuz-transit fee and Iranian port blockade announcement, triggering 'widespread risk-off sentiment.'

news.headline: Bulls snap losing streak as PSX gains 1,000 points during intraday trade
news.summary: Wednesday confirmed final close (published 05:05pm PKT): KSE-100 settled at 175,285.78, up 1,766.97 points (+1.02%) from Tuesday's close of 173,518.81; intraday high 176,701.38 at 10:02am, superseding the morning's 'Opening Bell' read logged earlier this cycle. Drivers cited: value buying after the prior session's steep declines (Mettis Global); Trump replacing the proposed 20% Strait of Hormuz transit toll with GCC investment commitments, per AKD Securities research director Awais Ashraf; softer-than-expected US inflation data easing concerns over further Fed rate hikes, supporting capital-flow outlook and the rupee; Brent crude +1.2% to $85.72/bbl and WTI +0.8% to $79.98/bbl on the continuing US naval blockade of Iranian ports and regional tensions. No specific tickers/sectors named in the source reviewed.

news.headline: PSX continues recovery as KSE-100 index gains 2,600 points in early trade
news.summary: Thursday morning (published/updated 11:11am PKT): KSE-100 at 177,890.27, up 2,604.49 points (+1.49%) from Wednesday's close of 175,285.78; Dawn attributes the continued rebound to 'value-hunting by equity investors' following Tuesday's panic-driven Strait-of-Hormuz selloff and Wednesday's partial recovery; no specific sectors or analysts named in the source reviewed.

news.headline: Textile exports stagnate at $17.9bn in FY26; June exports drop 16.71% YoY
news.summary: FY26 textile exports totalled $17.93bn, up just 0.26% YoY from $17.88bn in FY25 (Dawn) - 'one of the weakest performances in recent years' - missing the annual export target by $4.87bn, partly attributed to the suspension of trade with Afghanistan (an export market worth nearly $1.5bn); by product, readymade garments +3.87% in value, yarn +12.40%, knitwear -0.88%, cotton cloth -7.55%. Mettis Global's own figures: June 2026 textile exports were $1.27bn, down 16.71% YoY and 22.72% MoM (from $1.64bn in May), with knitwear -19.99%, readymade garments -12.43%, bed wear -23.29%; textile group products were 53.52% of total June exports. No individual company figures disclosed in either source.

news.headline: Large-Scale Manufacturing grows 5.77pc despite May slump
news.summary: LSM sector posted 5.77% YoY growth in the first 11 months (Jul-May) of FY26; QIM index 121.65 vs 115.02 in the corresponding prior-year period, though May alone contracted 0.98% YoY (+1.21% MoM vs April). Top contributors to growth: automobiles +1.53pp (production +58.82%), food products +1.36pp (output +7.75%), garments +1.20pp (exports +7.31%), petroleum products +0.78pp (coke and petroleum +10.56%). Detractors: pharmaceuticals -8.07%, iron & steel -7.49%, chemicals -2.64%, fertilizers -2.25%, textiles -0.09% - sector-level aggregate data only, no individual companies named in the source reviewed.

news.headline: PSX sets Rs925bn target for Jul-Sep 2026
news.summary: Published 10:14am PKT: PSX issued a revised Jul-Sep 2026 government-securities auction calendar, on the advice of the Debt Management Office (DMO) of the Ministry of Finance, targeting cumulative Rs925bn issuance of Government of Pakistan Hybrid Sukuk (GHS) and Ijarah Sukuk (GIS) - Rs625bn via Variable Rental Rate instruments across five auctions and Rs300bn via Fixed Rental Rate/Fixed Rate Zero Coupon structures across two auctions, tenors from 3-month to 10-year. This is a routine government debt-auction calendar administered via PSX, not a PSX-company revenue or earnings figure.

news.headline: Pakistan's FY26 import bill climbs 8.15%
news.summary: Published 10:11am PKT: FY26 import bill totalled $69.76bn (Rs19.59trn), up 8.15% YoY in dollar terms (8.72% in rupee terms) from $64.51bn (Rs18.02trn) in FY25. Breakdown by commodity group: petroleum $16.86bn (+5.76% YoY, largest contributor), food $9.15bn (+11.66%), metal $6.31bn (+12.07%), transport $4.06bn (+66.36%, sharpest growth); textile was the only major category to decline, at $6.46bn (-12.16% YoY).

news.headline: HBL unveils HBL PayPak UnionPay co-badge debit card; SBP governor hails launch
news.summary: HBL, described as Pakistan's largest debit-card issuer, launched the HBL PayPak UnionPay Co-Badge Debit Card at a ceremony at HBL Tower, Karachi, on Jul 15, 2026, developed with 1Link-operated PayPak and UnionPay International to combine domestic PayPak acceptance with UnionPay's international network on one card. SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad welcomed the launch as aligned with SBP's Vision 2028 and the 'Cashless Pakistan' agenda; no revenue, fee or volume figures for the card itself disclosed in the sources reviewed - reputational/strategic item for HBL, not caught in the prior checkpoint.

news.headline: Mobile banking users reach 137 million as digital payments surge
news.summary: Published 11:01am PKT, citing SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad: mobile banking users reached 137 million; retail digital transactions rose from 6.9bn to nearly 12bn over the past year; active merchants accepting digital payments rose from ~500,000 to over 2 million; remittances received via digital channels rose from 80% to 92%. Sector-wide digital-payments tailwind, no individual bank ticker figures disclosed.

news.source: Business Recorder / Express Tribune / PakTribune / Daily Patriot
news.headline: PSX extends rebound - KSE-100 up nearly 3,100 points by midday as oil stabilises
news.summary: Thursday afternoon, continuing from the morning's +2,604.49-point read already logged this cycle (previous close 175,285.78): Business Recorder reported the index at 178,378.43 as of 12:09pm, up 3,092.65 points (+1.76%); Express Tribune's midday report had it at 178,124.14, up 2,838.36 points (+1.62%), intraday high 178,431.73 / low 175,672.33, volume 144.6m shares worth Rs13.72bn; Daily Patriot reported an intraday high of 178,431.73 (+3,145.95 pts, +1.79%). Drivers: stabilising oil prices (Brent -0.5% to $84.50/bbl, still +11% for the week) as US-Iran Strait of Hormuz tensions eased, and softer US inflation data reducing Fed rate-hike fears; Business Recorder cited buying interest in automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil & gas exploration, OMCs, power generation and refinery; Daily Patriot noted an analyst comment that 'attention is shifting to the upcoming earnings season, which is expected to drive sector-specific activity.' No confirmed final closing-bell figure found in sources reviewed as of this cycle (17:00 PKT checkpoint) - flagged as the latest available intraday read pending a Closing Bell/DPS-confirmed print.
